title: The Eternal Return Chamber

features.name: the return stone
features.desc-on-touch: a weathered marker placed at the spot where the settlement's outer track circles back to itself; its surface holds tally marks, one for each cycle recorded

features.name: the settler's rest
features.desc-on-touch: a clearing where paths converge; worn flat by the returning steps of people who learned that departure and arrival were the same direction

features.name: the year-ring post
features.desc-on-touch: a wooden pole carved with concentric circles; each ring is a year; each year contains the same day visited multiple times; the carvings go deeper than the wood can reasonably hold

features.name: the cycle marker
features.desc-on-touch: a rope laid in a perfect circle on the ground, its ends meeting at a knot; the rope is old; the knot has been tied and untied so many times the fibres are soft

features.name: the convergence gate
features.desc-on-touch: two fence-lines meet here; they form an entrance and an exit that are positioned identically; you cannot tell which is which until you have walked through

features.name: the track that turns
features.desc-on-touch: the settler's path spirals tighter and tighter, mapping each return with a narrower circuit; at the centre it stops; nobody knows why they stopped walking inward

inscription: the settlement never left; it only learned to return; each leaving is a new arriving at the place you started

file.name: Settler_Route_Maps_1921_1987_Terracotta_Archive.txt
file.note: a handwritten log of settlement movements from the early decades; each entry records a departure and a return; the ink becomes darker with each cycle

exits.label: upward to where cycles first learned to breathe
into the convergence of all roads that remember where they started
to a place where the spiral tightens and arriving becomes indistinguishable from home
